pr_title: Report transport message size per action
pr_body:
Adds to the transport stats a histogram of transport message sizes for each transport action.

Closes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/88151
pr_comments: Hi @DaveCTurner, I've created a changelog YAML for you.
Hi @DaveCTurner, I've updated the changelog YAML for you.

issue_context.title: Track volume of transport traffic broken down by action/category
issue_context.body:
Today's transport stats include information on the total number of messages/bytes received/sent on each node. We occasionally get asked for more detail about the volume of transport traffic and it is not easy to give an accurate answer to this kind of question today.

I propose we break down these traffic volume stats by action (and distinguish requests from responses) to more easily answer this kind of question. We could alternatively group actions together into categories such as "indexing" and "search" and so on, but I think the extra detail would be useful sometimes and not terribly expensive to track. Maybe we should do both, because the categorised output would be much easier for end-users to consume.

It might be a bit tricky to add all the plumbing needed for this kind of breakdown. At the stage that we know the size of a message on the wire (after compression etc) we don't necessarily know its action, at least for responses, and indeed we may have no way to determine the action for a timed-out response. I think that's ok, these sorts of situations shouldn't happen often enough to matter for stats.

review_comments: Not sure I understand the difference, can you explain the motivation for changing this?
When `Version.CURRENT` becomes 9.0 we remove all the v7.x version constants, so by mentioning one here we are forced to remove this dead code to fix the compile error.

Would it be possible to distinguish the case of the action not found (which should always be a bug and seems ok to omit) from the case of a circuit breaker (or other) exception?

Something like still adding request and response stats if we can get a valid `requestHandlers.getHandler(action);`?

I'd find it nicer to include the circuit breaking exception responses in the tracking.
Sure, reworked in 905e5ad099a8d128039692c351bd99b7a395d541 to capture the stats whenever the action is known.
I am not sure I see a potential for exceptions in the code above. Fine to keep this, but if there is no exception expected, perhaps we can assert false here?
Yes I couldn't either but I'm paranoid about leaking a response here (or in future). Assertion added in 20ee73d39d6be64741dae30b3b12dd4991070808.
